scenes.sub: Convert every headline yield into an expected yield after the losses it statistically carries.

scenes.sub: risk-adjusted yield = headline − (annual loss probability × loss given default) − costs You don't know the true loss probability, so write down an assumption and be conservative. Newer protocols, more dependencies and higher leverage deserve higher numbers. Th
scenes.vo: risk-adjusted yield = headline minus (annual loss probability times loss given default) minus costs You don't know the true loss probability, so write down an assumption and be conservative. Newer protocols, more dependencies and higher leverage deserve higher numbers. The point isn't precision; it's making you compare positions on the same footing.
scenes.cap: risk-adjusted yield = headline − (annual loss probability × loss given default) − costs You don't know the true loss probability, so write down an assumption and be conservative. Newer protocols, more dependencies and higher leverage deserve higher numbers. The point isn't precision; it's making you compare positions on the same footing.

scenes.title: Worked example
scenes.vo: New protocol vault, 9.0%, 3% a year, 100%, 6.0%. Blue-chip lending, 4.5%, 0.5% a year, 100%, 4.0%.

scenes.sub: the calculator The 9% vault still wins on expectation, but by 2 points, not 4.5. Its bad outcome is also far worse, so size it smaller (Lesson 13.3).
